input.quote: Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification provision at all: the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties, ending at 19.5/p0075) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless", and "defend" return only incidental references. Section 9.3 expressly cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5", Section 21.3 carves out "its indemnification obligations" from the liability cap, 19.4 preserves remedies for "indemnified claims", and 30.5 refers to "vested indemnity rights" — all of which presuppose an indemnity section that does not exist. Per the playbook, absence of a Vendor indemnity is a critical deviation, so we inserted a new Section 20 covering third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, bodily injury/property damage, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at 20.5 (curing the dangling cross-reference). Customer's reciprocal indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's own breach of law, consistent with the preferred position; the usual Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions are included as a reasonable concession.

proposal.summary: Insert missing Section 20 (Indemnification): Vendor IP/law/data/misconduct indemnity, claim procedure, IP remedies, and a narrow Customer indemnity.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The agreement has no indemnification section even though Sections 9.3 and 21.3 assume one exists (9.3 cross-references "Section 20.5"), so we have inserted Section 20 giving us a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP claims, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and infringement remedies. Our reciprocal indemnity is deliberately narrow (Customer-provided content and our own breach of law); if helpful, we can accept the usual IP exclusions for Customer modifications, combinations and specifications.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to, use, or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor or its personnel, Affiliates, or subcontractors; (d) death, personal injury, or damage to tangible property caused by Vendor; or (e) Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.

Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim, and resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that content or materials Customer provides to Vendor infringe or misappropriate a third party's intellectual property right; or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Customer has no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement.

The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of a claim, provided that delay reduces the indemnifying Party's obligations only to the extent it is materially prejudiced. The indemnifying Party controls the defence and settlement with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified Party, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim in a manner that imposes a non-indemnified obligation or liability on, or admits fault by, the indemnified Party without its prior written consent.

Vendor's indemnity in Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables other than as authorized by Vendor, Customer's combination of the Services or Deliverables with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would not have arisen absent the combination, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.

If the Services or Deliverables are alleged or found to infringe, Vendor shall, at its expense and at Customer's election, procure the right for Customer to continue use, or modify or replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item. If neither remedy is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated period and Fees paid for affected Deliverables. These remedies are in addition to, and do not limit, Vendor's obligations under Section 20.1.
